## Context

Rebar has strong but manual mutation evidence for seven selected behavioral cores. The latest
recorded runs killed 99.2-100% of mapped mutants, but no gate prevents a changed test from
weakening those contracts. The operator selected targeted Gerrit Validate checks as the best
benefit/cost point; a broad sweep remains scheduled/manual to catch mapping and tool drift.

## Design

- Add one machine-readable shard manifest. Each shard owns one production module, its mapped
  test paths/globs, its mutmut module filter, and numeric result budgets. Config and tests must
  prove every current `only_mutate` and selected-test entry is represented.
- Add a stdlib Python driver that resolves `git diff HEAD^..HEAD` on a Gerrit patchset. A changed
  mapped source or test selects that shard; changes to mutation config, the manifest, runner, or
  lockfile select every shard. An unresolvable diff fails closed. No applicable shard is an
  explicit successful skip.
- Add a reusable mutation workflow. Gerrit Validate invokes targeted mode and includes its result
  in the `Verified` vote. A weekly/manual workflow invokes all-shards mode. Both check out the
  exact ref under test and always publish a machine-readable summary plus mutmut artifacts.
- Pin Python 3.12 and `mutmut==3.7.0`, run with `--max-children 1`, preserve the deterministic
  pytest selection, and set explicit per-mutant and 30-minute whole-job timeouts.
- Cache `mutants/` only under a key derived from the exact mutmut/Python versions and selected
  source, tests, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, shard manifest, and runner bytes. An exact hit never
  bypasses evaluation. Restored older state is advisory acceleration only: mapped test files are
  explicit mutmut cache-invalidation inputs and `on_dependency_change = "rerun"`.
- Run the selected clean tests before mutation. Then run only the selected mutmut module filters.
  Parse every status; zero mutants and unknown/not-checked/interrupted/segfault statuses fail.

## Historical per-shard budgets

| Shard | Killed floor | Survivor ceiling | No-tests ceiling | Timeout ceiling | Mapped-score floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| signing | 378 | 3 | 110 | 0 | 99.2% |
| reducer processors | 774 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 99.4% |
| next batch | 713 | 6 | 208 | 0 | 99.2% |
| gates | 557 | 0 | 376 | 0 | 100.0% |
| validate | 443 | 0 | 223 | 0 | 100.0% |
| compact policy | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100.0% |
| push policy | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100.0% |

The survivor/no-tests allowances are narrow, documented equivalent or subprocess-attribution
cases already explained in `docs/mutation-testing.md`; there is no global fuzzy severity or
project-wide score allowance. A source-changing patch may update a shard baseline only with the
new counts and rationale visible in the same review.

## False-positive and flakiness policy

- Baseline-test failure is reported as a test failure, never as a mutation survivor.
- Tool/setup failure, zero-mutant execution, and whole-job timeout are infrastructure/configuration
  failures, separate from mutation regressions. Only independently identified setup operations
  may retry; mutation outcomes never become green through retry.
- A new survivor, no-tests result, timeout, killed-count loss, or mapped-score loss is blocking.
  When any shard budget fails, every non-killed mutant in that shard is rerun once for diagnosis. The rerun cannot rescue the
  gate: a stable result is the mutation regression; a changed result is a nondeterminism failure
  requiring test stabilization.
- Existing equivalent mutants stay as per-shard numeric allowances with documented reasons. This
  matches maintained OSS practice and avoids tests that pin cosmetic implementation details.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Gerrit Validate selects exactly the shards owned by changed mapped source/test paths, selects
      all shards for mutation-infrastructure changes, succeeds explicitly when none apply, and
      blocks when the patchset parent/diff cannot be resolved.
- [ ] The mutation job is included in the Gerrit `Verified` aggregation; newer patchsets cancel
      stale runs through the existing workflow concurrency group.
- [ ] Python, mutmut, concurrency, cache inputs, per-mutant timeout formula, and whole-job timeout
      are pinned/bounded as specified above.
- [ ] Every selected shard passes its clean tests before mutation and produces at least one parsed
      mutant.
- [ ] Each shard enforces all five numeric budgets in the historical table and fails on every
      unexpected mutmut status.
- [ ] When a shard budget fails, all non-killed mutants are rerun once; the rerun never turns the gate green, and inconsistent outcomes
      are reported as nondeterminism failures.
- [ ] Results and artifacts distinguish skip, baseline-test, tool/setup, timeout, mutation
      regression, and nondeterminism outcomes.
- [ ] A weekly/manual broad run uses the same driver, manifest, budgets, and artifact format.
- [ ] Hermetic tests cover path-to-shard selection, manifest completeness, cache-key sensitivity,
      every result/failure class, baseline comparison, and Gerrit vote dependency.
- [ ] `docs/mutation-testing.md` documents both cadences, current verified results, allowed
      equivalent mutants, and the baseline-update review rule.

## Verification

    pytest -q tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py
    python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py
    make lint
    make typecheck

## Primary sources

- mutmut configuration, cache invalidation, timeouts, and explicit mutant reruns:
  https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
- PostHog targeted changed-source/test gate and exact-input cache:
  https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-python/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
- Instructor pinned tool, clean archive, hard timeout, and explicit survivor/timeout budgets:
  https://github.com/567-labs/instructor/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
- Trailmark PR/main execution and always-reported results:
  https://github.com/trailofbits/trailmark/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
- GeoParquet scheduled/manual sweep, setup-only retries, zero-mutant failure, and artifacts:
  https://github.com/geoparquet/geoparquet-io/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml
